answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a public contract before it can submit work; the bond is returned only after an independent reviewer validates a randomly sampled result. A false identity therefore needs its own funded bond, and fabricated work risks forfeiture, so creating thousands of sybils ties up capital and exposes it to loss. Reputation can signal reliable history, while a summit may set review rules and an atlas may map contribution records, but neither replaces the costly bond.
